items.note: A periwinkle band covers the page header, with a breadcrumb, a regular-weight 'Profile' h1, ink text and a pill sub-nav whose selected pill is filled white. Below it sits one outlined white card with the form in two columns, a square initials avatar and a save row: one pink 'Save changes' and a ghost 'Reset'. This matches the spec's Settings row (band and lift only).

The band collapses to the title and a pill strip, and 'Billing' is cut off at the edge to show the strip scrolls. The form is one column inside the outlined card, with the pink save button and ghost reset button kept in the flow. Nothing is cut off and the spacing is even.

Same layout on a black ground. The band keeps its periwinkle fill with ink text, the card is dark raised with a light border, the selected pill is a dark raised fill, and pink 'Save changes' is the only pink action. This follows the spec's dark mapping.

The mobile dark layout matches light: the band title, a scrolling pill strip with an ink-filled selected pill, the one-column form in a dark card, and the pink save button with an outlined reset button. Inputs and labels are legible.

Under the band (title, count line, pill sub-nav with 'Notifications' selected) sit two outlined cards, Email and Push. Each has hairline-ruled toggle rows with an 'On'/'Off' text label next to an ink switch. There is no pink, and the hierarchy is clear: band, then card titles, then rows.
The two cards stack in one column. Each row's label and description wrap on the left, with the On/Off text and switch on the right. The rhythm between rows is even and nothing touches the card edges.

The dark version keeps the periwinkle band with ink text and a dark-filled selected pill. The cards are dark raised with light borders, and the switches are light when on and outlined when off, each with a text label, so state does not rely on color alone.
Same stacked cards on black, with readable descriptions and switches. The pill strip shows 'Notifications' as an ink pill and lets 'Billing' run off the edge as a scroll cue.

A two-column layout below the band: an outlined 'Change password' card with one pink 'Update password' button, and an 'Active sessions' table in a bordered box. The table has an ink header rule, a 'This device' outline pill and small outlined Revoke row actions.

The sessions table now reflows into stacked blocks in its bordered box: each has the device as its title, Location and Last active as label/value lines, and a Revoke button that is visible, which fixes the earlier hidden-column major. The block titles are set in a heavier weight than the regular-only type rule allows.
The dark version of the two-column security layout: a dark password card with a pink submit, and a sessions table with a light header rule and outlined Revoke actions. Text contrast holds throughout.

The stacked session blocks hold in dark mode with every Revoke visible, and the pink 'Update password' is the only pink action. As in light, the device-name block titles are heavier than regular weight.

Three outlined plan cards, each with a pink price tag and check-mark features. The current plan has a heavier outline and a 'Current plan' status pill, the other plans have ghost switch buttons, and there are no pink actions. Below are a payment-method card and an invoices table with Due/Paid status pills that carry icons.

The plan cards stack, and the invoices reflow into stacked blocks (title, then Date/Amount/Status lines) inside one bordered box, so nothing is hidden. The invoice IDs used as block titles are set heavier than regular weight.

The dark version keeps the pink price tags as the only pink, with dark plan cards, a lighter outline on the current plan, and an invoices table with a light header rule and outlined status pills. It is clean and readable.
Stacked plan cards, payment method and invoice blocks on black with even card gaps. The status pills with icons stay legible, and nothing overflows at phone width.

findings.summary: When phone-width tables reflow into stacked blocks, each block's title (session device name, invoice ID) is set in a semibold or bold weight. This breaks the regular-weight-only type rule; the spec allows bold only for totals and inline emphasis.
